superficial: It seems a wormhole pulled me through… ship and all.
This system isn't mine. The star is old and the light is amber.
From what I read at the Institute, I think I'm in the home system of the Absent.
A ring of stone and metal, dark. Across the arch runs a crack of light that slowly closes behind your back.
Every time you wake up, you are here.
profunda: Now you see the crack differently: it is not closing, it is being sewn shut.
Something, somewhere, keeps this quarter of an hour open.

superficial: INAUGURATION OF THE MOUTH
By leave of the Transit Council, and to the pride of one and all, the first passage to the sibling worlds opens today.
profunda: Underneath, in small letters and in a different hand, someone engraved: "The count begins today."
Now you know that the clocks drift apart. A count, then: of what?

superficial: Two columns written in the same hand: "Threshold" and "Archive".
At first the hours match. Page after page, the second falls behind, a little more each day.
Nobody wrote down why.
Crates, barrels, letters. Destination of all: —.
No name, no map, no coordinates.
profunda: The receipts from that destination arrive with dates that barely advance: for each day here, a blink there.
Now you know how to read it: it is a place where time hardly runs.

umbral.hoja_entrada.titulo: A loose sheet from the register
superficial: Shipments to the Archive. The cargo would not go in through the glass: nobody could break it.
"Under the third tower, at the bottom, the door of the shaft. Look for the three bands."
"Dearest: every evening I come to the stone bench and set out two cups. Tell me you have eaten, that you sleep, that you do not work late..."
There is no signature. The second cup is clean.
profunda: At the bottom, in different ink: "You write that for you a week has passed. Here, months have."
Whoever waited knew that the time of the one who left ran differently.

superficial: Inscriptions by children, made in charcoal: numbers, and below them the way to write the hours.
You learn to read the clock of the Absent.
profunda: In the corner, a lullaby written to learn the rhythm:
"Sleep, sleep, never cross the same Gate twice in the same day."

superficial: Six houses. The tables are still set. There are no signs of violence.
profunda: A notice nailed to a door. Now you can read the hour: "Evacuation. Forty minutes. Gates 2 to 6."
The tables are still set because nobody had time.

superficial: The Mouth opens for an instant. Its light reaches other worlds.
Something, very far away, called it; and it answered.
A full-length carved figure, much taller than you: almost twice an Ool.
It has no face. The head is an oval of dark glass with inlaid diamonds that still glow; copper threads run across its skin, smooth as porcelain.
Above it, the ring of a Gate. This is how they saw themselves: this is what the Absent were like.
The screen is still on standby. When you touch it, a map lights up: lines of light that all start here and reach every world of the system.
Next to this point, a single word repeated on every line: «Origin».
This was not just another post. The first Gate was opened from here: you are in the home of the Absent.
The chisels are sorted by size, except one, dropped next to the cup. The tea dried at the bottom.
On the panel, the figure is carved down to the waist; above, the guide lines are still waiting.
Whoever worked here didn't finish. They put down the chisel and left.
profunda: Now you know about the notice: forty minutes.
There wasn't even time to put the tools away.

superficial: Four bronze bells hang from a crossbar, as if waiting for someone to carry them off.
They weigh what a full jug weighs. None has a number or a mark: all four are alike.
A stone channel, sloping, with sixteen bronze marks along it. At the top, a stop.
Every twenty seconds a bronze ball sets off down it, faster and faster.
A bell would fit on each mark. If they stood at equal distances, they would ring closer and closer together.
A strip of slate under the board in the Classroom. Above, sixteen little marks in a row; below, a rhyme in a child's handwriting:
“The ball counts one, counts four, counts nine… and the next one, where does it fall?”
Three marks are filled with amber chalk: the first, the fourth and the ninth. The next one is empty.
A sandstone lectern with its lid closed and a slit of light beneath it.
From the mechanism below comes, now and then, a small tap, like someone waiting for their turn.

umbral.hoja_carga.titulo: The loading sheet of the silos
superficial: A loading sheet nailed to a post, at the foot of the silos on the Dock.
“For the cistern of the Archive: ballast up to the third mark, seven parts of stone. Wood is no use: it floats.”
